overall: The AG found two violations: the July 22 notice's "Policy 66 Complaint" topic was insufficiently specific, and the Board voted to approve a Town Manager contract in executive session on August 15. The August 26 open-session announcement did not cure the vote, and nullification was declined. Other allegations were rejected or withdrawn.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the July 22 notice topic 'Policy 66 Complaint' was not specific enough; minutes show the topic was discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Because notice of the July 22 meeting did not reasonably inform the public of a topic that was discussed, we find the notice insufficiently specific, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the July 22 notice had typographical errors ('Town Hall Ro', 'Jih 18 2025') that made it misleading.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, we do not find that these errors rendered the notice insufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the July 22 notice's reference to the July 23 executive session gave insufficient notice of that session.
allegations.key_passage: Where the July 23 meeting was the subject of separate, adequate notice, and the reference to it in the notice of the July 22 meeting was for informational purposes only, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the July 23 executive session notice was vague because it referenced collective bargaining, litigation, and detriment to open meetings, none of which was discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Where the notice makes it clear to the public that the Board would discuss contract negotiations with the Town Manager at the meeting, and that is indeed what was discussed, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the July 23 notice did not list an open session before the executive session and was ambiguous about public access.
allegations.key_passage: Although imperfect, this language satisfies the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the July 23 notice did not make clear that the open session was accessible to the public or explain why it was not broadcast.
allegations.key_passage: making it accessible to interested members of the public.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the August 12 executive session notice had the same superfluous references to bargaining, litigation, and open-session detriment.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons set forth in Section II above, we find no violation as to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the August 12 open-session discussion of the Acting Town Manager's performance review lacked Purpose 1 safeguards such as 48-hour notice to the subject.
allegations.key_passage: The Board discussed the performance review in open session, as it was required to do,

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Board voted in executive session on August 15 to execute a contract with the Town Manager, which must be done in open session.
allegations.key_passage: By voting to approve the contract with the Town Manager in executive session on August 15, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board argued that announcing the contract at its August 26 open meeting cured the executive session vote; the AG rejected the cure argument.
allegations.key_passage: The Board could have remedied the violation by voting on the contract in open session.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that actions taken in violation of the Law be nullified; the AG declined to nullify.
allegations.key_passage: Prior to the August 16 swearing in of the Town Manager, the Board had at least put the public on notice of negotiations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a failure to address minute taking and review, which the AG declined to review as unclear and unspecific.
Complaint alleged the July 23 notice failed to note the date and time of posting, but the complainant withdrew that allegation.
allegations.key_passage: The complainant also alleged that the Board failed to note the date and time of posting the notice for the July 23 meeting but withdrew that allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the August 15 notice had typos, did not clearly state an open session, and implied attendance was limited to Board members; the AG found no violation.
allegations.key_passage: As to the other violations alleged relative to the August 15 meeting,9 we find no violation for the reasons discussed above.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
